faqs.q: How is a travel nurse salary calculated?
faqs.a: A travel nurse salary is typically based on the hourly rate under the Nurses Award (MA000034) multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year. For example, a Registered Nurse Level 1 pay point 1 earns $32.09 per hour, giving an annual gross of about $63,400. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, raising the hourly rate to $40.11. Superannuation of 12% is paid on top of ordinary earnings, and income tax is deducted according to the 2026–27 resident tax scale.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for travel nurses?
faqs.a: Under the Nurses Award, casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. For a Registered Nurse Level 1 pay point 1, the base rate is $32.09 per hour, so the casual rate becomes $40.11 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. The National Minimum Wage also includes a 25% casual loading, bringing the casual rate to $33.05 per hour for award-free employees.

faqs.q: How does superannuation affect a travel nurse salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (the super guarantee rate from 1 July 2026). For a travel nurse earning $63,400 annually, the employer would contribute an additional $7,608 to super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not included in your take-home pay but is a key part of your total remuneration. Use [the timesheet](/) to see your super estimate alongside your gross pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Travel Nurse Salary

If you're a travel nurse working in Australia, your pay is likely governed by the **Nurses Award 2020** (MA000034) or the **National Minimum Wage** if you're award-free. Understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential for budgeting and comparing job offers. This guide explains the key components of a travel nurse salary, including award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax.

### The Formula: Hourly Rate × Hours per Week × 52

The standard full-time week for nurses under the Nurses Award is 38 ordinary hours. To calculate your annual gross pay:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, a **Registered Nurse Level 1 pay point 1** earns **$32.09 per hour** (from the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guide ). That gives:
- Weekly: $1,219.50
- Fortnightly: $2,439.00 (weekly × 2)
- Annual: $63,414.00 (before tax and super)

If you are a casual travel nurse, you receive a **25% casual loading** on top of the base rate. That makes your hourly rate **$40.11**, weekly **$1,524.38**, and annual **$79,267.76**.

Use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box to see your own figures.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. This applies only to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Travel nurses are almost always covered by the Nurses Award, which sets higher minimum rates. For instance, an Enrolled Nurse pay point 1 earns **$30.00 per hour**, and a Registered Nurse with a degree earns **$33.51 per hour**. Always check your classification in the award to ensure you're paid correctly.

Award rates are updated annually following the Fair Work Commission's Annual Wage Review. The 2026 data is available in the Modern Awards Pay Database.

### Casual Loading and Penalty Rates

Casual employees under the Nurses Award receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. This is in addition to any penalty rates for working weekends, public holidays, or night shifts. For example, a Registered Nurse Level 1 working Saturday earns **$48.14 per hour** (150% of base) and on Sunday **$56.16 per hour** (175%). Penalty rates are calculated on the base rate, not the casual rate. See [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) for more details.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay **superannuation guarantee** at **12%** of your ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026). This is paid on top of your gross salary, not deducted from it. For a travel nurse earning $63,414 annually, the employer contributes an additional **$7,609.68** to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of **$270,830**. Super is not part of your take-home pay but is a valuable long-term benefit. Learn about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus a **2% Medicare levy** (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). For a travel nurse earning $63,414, the estimated tax is about $9,064 and Medicare $1,268, leaving a take-home of around $53,082. Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for a detailed estimate.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many travel nurses are paid fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly rate multiplied by two. For the RN Level 1 example, that's **$2,439.00** before tax and super. After tax and Medicare, the take-home fortnightly is approximately **$2,041**. This can help you plan rent, bills, and savings.

### Comparing Job Offers

When comparing travel nurse salary offers, look at the hourly rate, whether it includes casual loading, and what penalty rates apply. The award minimums are a floor; some agencies pay above award. Use [pay guides](/blog) to find the correct classification for your role. Also check [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for context: the ABS reports full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings of **$2,083.70** (May 2026), which is higher than the award rate for many nurses.

### Summary

Your travel nurse salary is built from your award classification, hours, and loadings. Use the formula **hourly × 38 × 52** for annual gross, add 25% if casual, then add 12% super on top. Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home. Always verify your pay against the Nurses Award and the National Minimum Wage. For a quick calculation, try [the timesheet](/) – it handles the math for you.

*Disclaimer: Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.*
